# Intake brief — When player shoots enemy bullet it should explode

## Problem statement

When a player bullet intercepts an enemy bullet, both projectiles are destroyed **silently** — there is no sound effect (SFX) and no visual effect (VFX) at the point of impact. The player gets no feedback that an incoming shot was successfully shot down, so the interception reads as a missed/ignored collision rather than a skill-rewarding action.

## Users

- **Player** — wants clear, satisfying feedback when they shoot down an incoming enemy bullet.
  - *As a player, when my bullet destroys an enemy bullet I hear and see a small impact, so I know my shot connected and the threat is gone.*
- **Developer / designer** — wants one shared implementation used by both the shipped game and the gym scenes.
  - *As a developer, I want the bullet-impact feedback implemented in shared code so the game (`PlayScene`) and the gyms (`GymFormationScene`) cannot drift apart.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Dedicated bullet-destruction SFX.** When a player bullet overlaps an enemy bullet, a **new dedicated** `playBulletDestructionSound()` plays exactly once at the impact point. The shared enemy-destruction `playDestructionSound()` is **not** invoked for this event. Verified by a unit test spying on the audio module.
- [ ] **AC2 — Small impact VFX.** A small, short-lived flash/glow VFX appears at the impact point and is cleaned up when it finishes. The full `spawnExplosionParticles()` particle burst is **not** used for bullet destruction. Verified by a unit test asserting the impact effect is created and torn down.
- [ ] **AC3 — Shared code path (no game/gym divergence).** The bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback is implemented in a single shared helper/module and invoked by **both** `PlayScene._handleCollisions()` (case 2) and `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` (case 2) — the behaviour is identical in the shipped game and the gym. Verified by both call sites referencing the shared helper and by a test in each scene suite.
- [ ] **AC4 — No double feedback on player hit.** When an enemy bullet instead reaches the player, only the existing `_hitPlayer()` feedback fires; the enemy bullet is not also given the bullet-destruction SFX/VFX. Verified by a regression test.
- [ ] **AC5 — Test coverage (validation).** New/updated unit tests assert: the dedicated SFX fires once per interception (and not the generic cue); the impact VFX is created and cleaned up; both scenes route through the shared helper; and no double-play on player hit. Identical inputs remain deterministic.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (VFX) and §7.3 (SFX event catalogue) must record the new bullet-destruction cue.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite (`/skill:test`) and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- **Dedicated cue.** The new SFX must be a *new* function in `src/audio/effects.ts` (per producer decision), synthesised with the existing `blip()` helper. Short, higher-pitched and low-volume so it reads as a light "tick" and does not mask the heavier destruction cue. Must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests / autoplay-blocked browsers).
- **Small VFX only.** Bullets are ~3 px radius; the effect must be a brief flash/glow, **not** the full particle-burst system (`spawnExplosionParticles()` is explicitly out per producer answer Q2).
- **No feedback on player hit.** Do **not** add a separate explosion when the enemy bullet reaches the player — `_hitPlayer()`'s SFX + VFX already covers that collision (producer answer Q3).
- **Shared implementation.** Implement through a shared helper/module so `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` exercise the same code (producer follow-up #2: "They should share all code"). Do not add two divergent copies.
- **Narrow refactor.** Extract only what is needed for the bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback. Do not consolidate the wider duplicated collision logic here — that is tracked separately in AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO.
- Preserve all existing collision semantics, hit radii (`PLAYER_BULLET_RADIUS`, enemy-bullet radius 5) and consumption behaviour (both bullets are destroyed).

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._handleCollisions()` case 2 (player bullets vs enemy bullets) destroys both bullets with no SFX/VFX (~`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` line 1018).
- `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` case 2 has the identical silent behaviour (~`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` line 1463).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes `playDestructionSound()` (0.28 s sawtooth sweep, volume 0.3) and the reusable `blip()` synthesis helper. There is **no** bullet-destruction sound.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` exposes `spawnExplosionParticles()` for full particle bursts (used for entity/player destruction).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 lists "Player bullet hits enemy — Very short tick, Low volume" but has no bullet-vs-bullet entry; §7.2 covers particle explosions.
- There is no shared combat/collision module: the only two `_handleCollisions` implementations live in the two scenes above.

## Desired change

- Add a dedicated `playBulletDestructionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` (short, higher-pitched, low-volume blip).
- Add a small impact-VFX helper (e.g. a brief flash/glow graphic that fades and destroys itself) — a new shared module such as `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`.
- Extract a shared bullet-vs-bullet impact helper (e.g. `resolveBulletVsBulletImpact(scene, x, y)`) that plays the cue and spawns the VFX, and call it from case 2 of **both** `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` when a player bullet consumes an enemy bullet.
- Add/update unit tests for the SFX, the VFX, and both call sites; update the GDD §7.2/§7.3 documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playBulletDestructionSound()`; export any tuning constants.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` (new) — Shared small flash/glow impact VFX helper.
- `src/scenes/combat/` or equivalent (new, if preferred) — Shared bullet-vs-bullet impact resolution helper used by both scenes.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Call the shared helper in `_handleCollisions()` case 2.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Call the shared helper in `_handleCollisions()` case 2.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Assert the new cue's synthesis/no-op behaviour.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Assert dedicated SFX fired once, VFX spawned, no generic cue, no double-play on player hit.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Assert the same shared behaviour in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §7.2 (VFX) and §7.3 (SFX event catalogue).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "dedicated" means a new exported sound function, not reuse of `playDestructionSound()`.
- **Assumption:** "simpler VFX" means a brief flash/glow — no particle burst — and it need not be extensible to entities.
- **Risk — audio cacophony:** dense bullet patterns can produce many interceptions; the cue must be short and low-volume to avoid stacking (see GDD §6.7 SFX rate-limiting).
- **Risk — shared-helper placement:** both scenes are large; extracting into a clearly named shared module avoids a new divergent copy. Keep the change surgical.
- **Risk — scope creep:** the duplicated `_handleCollisions` logic in the two scenes is a wider problem; it is deliberately excluded and tracked in **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** so this item stays focused.
- **Risk — test coupling:** scene suites boot Phaser; assert via the shared helper and audio-module spies rather than pixel-level VFX inspection.

## Related work

Manual (genuinely relevant):

- **AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH** — Add randomness to explosion (in-progress, high): touches the same `playDestructionSound()`/explosion SFX area; the new bullet cue should not conflict with its randomisation scope.
- **AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M** — Restore gym-game parity (completed, epic): the RCA that established gym/game parity as a recurring concern; this item follows the same "prefer shared code" constraint.
- **AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB** / **AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH** — Core scene collision tests/implementation (completed): cover player-bullet-destroys-enemy-bullet behaviour without feedback.
- **AH-0MU4KJZUE001X6LD** — Extract shared bullet creation utility function (completed): precedent for shared bullet utilities.
- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Consolidate duplicated PlayScene/GymFormationScene collision logic (open, discovered-from this item): the wider duplication this item deliberately does not tackle.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** – Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x scale and cost a life (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNI1Y001O2OV** – Test: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_09_22.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, explosions, player (+5 more)
- `README.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, player, sfx (+3 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, player, sfx (+3 more)

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (asked 2026-09-16, answered 2026-09-17):

- **Q1 — SFX: reuse `playDestructionSound()` or a distinct cue?**
  Answer: **same** — reuse the existing `playDestructionSound()` (shared with enemy entities). *Superseded (see follow-up Q1).*
- **Q2 — VFX: existing `spawnExplosionParticles()` burst or a simpler effect?**
  Answer (producer): **simpler** — not the full particle burst; a brief flash or glow is preferred, given bullets are ~3 px radius. Research: `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` `spawnExplosionParticles()` is a size-scaled full burst (base count 30, clamped 8–80) — visually too heavy for a 3 px bullet.
- **Q3 — Scope: should the enemy bullet also explode when it hits the player?**
  Answer (producer): **no** — the existing `_hitPlayer()` SFX + VFX for the player is sufficient at the collision point.
- **Q4 — Consistency: dedicated sound or the generic one?**
  Answer: **dedicated** — bullet destruction should have its own dedicated sound cue, not reuse `playDestructionSound()`. *(Conflicted with Q1; see follow-up Q1.)*

Follow-up round (asked 2026-09-22, answered 2026-09-22) — resolves the Q1/Q4 contradiction:

- **Follow-up Q1 — Which SFX answer wins, Q1 ("same") or Q4 ("dedicated")?**
  Answer (producer): **Dedicated.** Create a bullet-specific cue — do not reuse `playDestructionSound()`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Follow-up Q2 — Scope: shipped game only, or should the gym core be mirrored?**
  Answer (producer): "There shouldn't be different core code in the shipped game and the gym scenes. They should share all code." Source: interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each define their own `_handleCollisions` (no shared combat module), so the impact feedback must be delivered through a shared helper used by both; wider consolidation of the duplicated collision logic is a separate follow-up (AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO, discovered-from this item).

Open questions: none — all clarifications answered.

# Leaderboard: Game-Over Score Entry and localStorage Display

## Problem Statement

The game currently has no scoring system, no game-over screen, and no leaderboard. When the player runs out of lives, the game respawns infinitely with no termination. The player has no way to record or view their high scores.

## Users

- **Player**: Completes the game (or dies) and wants to record their score by entering 3-character initials. They want to see their scores ranked against previous attempts on the game-over screen and from the main menu.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I run out of lives, I want to see my final score and be prompted to enter my initials so I can record my achievement.
- As a player, after entering my initials, I want to see the full leaderboard ranked by score so I can see how I compare to my past scores.
- As a player, from the main menu, I want to view the leaderboard to see my best scores.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Score tracking**: Each enemy type has a defined `scoreValue`. When an enemy is destroyed, its `scoreValue` is added to the player's total score. The score is displayed in the HUD (top-right corner, neon-styled numeric display).

2. **Game-over condition**: When the player's lives reach 0 (starting at 3, max 5 via P8 Extra Life), the game stops respawning and transitions to the game-over screen. There is no continue mechanic. The game-over screen shows the final score, an option to save (if score qualifies), and a restart button.

3. **Initials entry**: On the game-over screen, the player is prompted to enter exactly 3 uppercase letters (A-Z) as initials. Input is validated (only A-Z accepted, exactly 3 characters). [ASSUMPTION: on-screen clickable keyboard styled to match the neon terminal aesthetic.]

4. **localStorage persistence**: Entries are stored in browser localStorage under the key `ai_hell_leaderboard`. The stored data is a JSON array of entry objects (max 10 entries). When a new score qualifies for the leaderboard (i.e., would rank within the top 10), the player can enter initials to save it. If the score does not qualify, the player is informed and may skip the entry.

5. **Leaderboard display**: The game-over screen displays the full leaderboard showing rank, initials, score, and date for each entry, sorted by score (highest first). The leaderboard is also accessible from the main menu.

## Constraints

- Browser `localStorage` only (no backend, per GDD §5.1 — "single-machine" MVP).
- Maximum 10 leaderboard entries.
- Initials must be exactly 3 characters, uppercase letters only.
- Date format: ISO YYYY-MM-DD (per GDD data model example).
- The leaderboard data structure must support future abstraction for online leaderboards (GDD §5.3 migration note).

## Existing State

- **No score tracking exists**: No `scoreValue` on enemies, no score counter, no score display.
- **No game-over condition**: The `GymFormationScene` has infinite respawn — when all enemies are wiped, the formation respawns regardless of player lives.
- **Lives tracking exists**: `EffectsRegistry` tracks lives (starts at 3, caps at 5), displayed via the HUD. But lives are never decremented on player death.
- **No main menu**: The only entry scene is `GymIndex` (dev-mode gym scene launcher). No `MainMenuScene` exists.
- **No leaderboard code**: No localStorage operations for leaderboard, no initials input, no game-over screen.
- **GDD references**: `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts` are predicted but not yet implemented.

## Desired Change

1. **`src/core/Leaderboard.ts`** — Leaderboard persistence module:
   - `getEntries()`: Read and parse entries from localStorage.
   - `addEntry(initials: string, score: number)`: Add a new entry, maintain max 10, sort by score.
   - `getTopN(n: number)`: Return top N entries.
   - `isQualifying(score: number)`: Check if score would make the top 10.
   - Data structure: `{ rank, initials, score, date }` per GDD §5.2.

2. **Score tracking in `GymFormationScene`**:
   - Assign `scoreValue` to each enemy type (Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50 per, Boss: 1000 — [ASSUMPTION values, to be confirmed]).
   - Track player score as a counter in the scene.
   - Add score to total on enemy destroy.
   - Display score in the HUD (top-right).

3. **Game-over screen (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`)**:
   - Displays final score, player initials input, and leaderboard.
   - Neon-styled UI matching the game aesthetic.
   - On-screen 3x3 grid keyboard for initials entry.
   - "Submit" button validates and saves the entry.
   - "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex for now).

4. **Main menu (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`)**:
   - "Play" button to start the game.
   - "Leaderboard" button to view the full leaderboard.
   - "Gym" button to access the gym index.
   - [NOTE: Main menu creation scope — see open questions.]

5. **Lives integration**:
   - Decrement lives on player hit (when invulnerable period ends).
   - When lives reach 0, transition to game-over screen.
   - Stop the respawn loop when game-over is triggered.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope risk — main menu creation**: Creating a full main menu scene is a significant addition. If scope is constrained, the leaderboard may be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead, with the main menu deferred to a separate work item.
- **Scope risk — score tracking from scratch**: No score infrastructure exists. Implementing scoreValue on all enemy types, the score counter, and HUD display adds non-trivial work to GymFormationScene.
- **Assumption — enemy score values**: The GDD defines `scoreValue` on enemies but does not specify numeric values. The values in the draft are estimates and should be tuned.
- **Assumption — keyboard UI**: On-screen clickable keyboard was assumed; a producer decision is needed on input mechanism.
- **Assumption — game-over restart flow**: "Restart" returns to main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu). No "Play Again" shortcut from game-over.
- **Scope guard**: Level progression, boss mechanics, difficulty scaling, online leaderboards, and persistent game state between sessions are out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` — New file: leaderboard localStorage persistence
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — New file: game-over screen with initials input and leaderboard display
- `src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts` — New file: main menu with leaderboard access [scope TBD]
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Modify: add score tracking, game-over condition, lives decrement
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Modify: add score display (top-right)
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` / `src/entities/*.ts` — Modify: add `scoreValue` to enemy types
- `src/core/Game.ts` — Modify: register new scenes, update boot flow
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Modify: add MainMenu/GameOver to scene list for shipped build

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTZWZ1MQ004L552**: Create a playable game (parent epic, high priority, in `idea` stage) — includes main menu and playable game scope. This work item is a child of this epic.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **AH-0MU6VSKZT006HBTR**: Leaderboard — discovered-from the playable-game epic; the GDD (§5) is the authoritative spec.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.
- **GDD §6.4**: Technical architecture — predicted `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts`.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes (gym scenes where power-up layer is shared) — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q1**: Main menu scope — Should this work item include creating the Main Menu scene (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`), or should that be a separate work item? The GDD references `src/ui/Menu.ts` ("Main menu, game-over screen") but it has not been implemented. The leaderboard must be "accessible from the main menu" per the work item description. **Assumption**: This work item creates the main menu scene with leaderboard access. If the producer disagrees, the main menu creation should be a separate work item, and the leaderboard should be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead (or from the game-over screen itself).

- **Q2**: Score tracking scope — Should this work item include implementing score tracking from scratch (enemy `scoreValue` assignment, score counter, HUD display, points on destroy), or should score tracking be a prerequisite completed by a separate work item? **Assumption**: Score tracking is included in scope — it is fundamental to the leaderboard feature.

- **Q3**: Initials input mechanism — How should the 3-character initials entry work? Options: (a) on-screen clickable keyboard (A-Z grid, neon-styled), (b) browser-native text input styled with CSS, (c) other mechanism. **Assumption**: On-screen clickable keyboard matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q4**: Enemy `scoreValue` values — What point values should each enemy type carry? Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm (per-unit), Boss? **Assumption**: Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50, Boss: 1000. These can be tuned later via the game-rules config.

- **Q5**: Score format — Should the score display show formatted numbers (e.g., "50,000") or raw (e.g., "50000")? **Assumption**: Raw numeric display (no commas) matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q6**: Game-over flow — After submitting a score (or declining to submit), should the game-over screen offer a "Restart" button that returns to the main menu, or should it auto-restart? **Assumption**: "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu exists). "Play Again" is not available until a score is submitted or declined.

# Intake Brief — Need juice when the player is destroyed (AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY)

> **Status of this brief:** the operator was asked four clarifying questions
> (see Appendix) and replied "continue" without answering. Per the workflow's
> "do not block indefinitely" rule, this brief proceeds on **documented
> assumptions** (marked `[ASSUMPTION]` throughout). Open questions are retained
> in the Appendix for producer validation; the item is flagged
> `needsProducerReview` until they are resolved.

## Problem statement

When the player is destroyed the game currently plays a single particle burst
(`spawnExplosionParticles(...SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE...)`), the shared enemy
`playDestructionSound()`, and a 150% scale pulse, then immediately respawns or
ends the run. There is no camera shake, no player-specific death sound, and no
layered secondary feedback, so the most consequential event in the game feels
flat. The operator wants "lots of juice … screen shake, particle explosion, SFX
etc. Go wild!"

## Users

- **Player** — feels a weighty, unmistakable consequence when their ship is
  destroyed, distinct from ordinary enemy kills, reinforcing that a life was
  lost (or the run ended).
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — can adjust shake intensity, sound
  layering, flash strength, and extra layers through exposed constants in one
  place without editing each death path.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, when my ship is destroyed I feel a strong impact: the
  camera shakes hard, a bright flash frames the screen, the explosion is
  visibly larger than an enemy's, and a distinct low "hull breach" boom plays
  instead of the generic enemy pop — so a life lost reads differently from a
  kill.
- As a **player**, the effect scales: losing my final life (game over) feels
  even heavier than a mid-run respawn, without becoming disorienting.
- As a **developer**, I can tune `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, and the dedicated sound's amplitude in one
  constants module, and the behaviour is covered by unit tests so tuning does
  not silently regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Shared player-death juice helper exists:** A reusable helper
  (e.g. `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` or an extension of
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) can be invoked from a scene with
  `(scene, x, y)` and composes the full effect (screen shake + particle burst +
  flash + any additional layers), returning/recording handles so scene teardown
  can destroy them. Both player-death paths use it:
  `PlayScene._loseLife()` (real run, lives/game-over) and
  `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (combat gym, in-place respawn).
- [ ] **AC2 — Screen shake:** A scene-camera shake is triggered on player
  destruction with a configurable intensity and duration (suggested defaults:
  intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms, full 2D). Shake strength is a
  tunable constant in one module. Verified by unit test with a camera spy
  (`camera.shake` called with the configured intensity/duration).
- [ ] **AC3 — Dedicated player-death SFX:** A new `playPlayerDestructionSound()`
  in `src/audio/effects.ts`, distinct from the generic
  `playDestructionSound()` (suggested: heavier/lower multi-layer cue — impact
  thump + descending body + brief noise tail), exposed amplitude/length as
  constants. The player-death paths call it **exactly once**; existing
  `playDestructionSound()` calls on those paths are replaced (no double-play).
  Verified by unit test (call-count + no generic sound on player death).
- [ ] **AC4 — Extra juice layers (assumption-marked):** At least two additional
  layered effects beyond particles + shake + sound, each configurable and
  testable. Proposed set `[ASSUMPTION]`: (a) a brief full-screen white/cyan
  **flash** (alpha fades ~1 → 0 over ~120–200 ms) and (b) **debris shards** or
  an expanding **shockwave ring** that outlive the particle burst briefly. Each
  layer is individually toggleable via a constant so the producer can drop any
  they dislike without code surgery.
- [ ] **AC5 — Severity scaling & no behaviour change:** The effect is heavier
  for run-ending death (final life / game over) than for a mid-run respawn
  `[ASSUMPTION]`, via a `severity` parameter. Respawn position, invulnerability
  duration, blink, lives/score accounting, and shield-absorption behaviour are
  unchanged; no changes to hit detection.
- [ ] **AC6 — Teardown / no leaks:** All juice-owned GameObjects (flash
  overlay, debris, shockwave, particles) are tracked and destroyed on scene
  `SHUTDOWN`; stop→restart of a scene instance leaks nothing (mirrors the
  existing `playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: shake fired with
  configured params; dedicated sound called exactly once and generic sound not
  called on the player path; flash fades and is destroyed; debris/shockwave
  lifecycle; severity scaling; teardown leaks nothing. Existing player/scene
  suites still pass (update any assertions that assume the old single-burst
  behaviour).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** GDD §7.2 (and §7.3 audio if the new cue is
  listed) updated to describe the player-death juice; code comments on new
  constants/helpers; README updated if it documents audio/VFX behaviour.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**
  (`npm test` = `vitest run`) and `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`).

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser 4.2.1 + TypeScript 7, Vite, Vitest 4 (existing stack).
  Prefer Phaser `camera.shake()` for shake and Graphics/tween layers for the
  rest, consistent with the existing Graphics-particle approach in
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`.
- **Performance:** must not drop FPS on web; layers are short-lived and pooled
  or destroyed promptly; no per-frame allocation leaks.
- **Neon aesthetic:** consistent with GDD §7.1 palette; player effects centre
  on `SHIP_COLOR 0x00ffff`.
- **No behaviour change beyond VFX/audio:** respawn, invulnerability, lives,
  score, and shield logic untouched; no double audio.
- **Testability:** pure logic (intensity/duration/severity mapping) separated
  from Phaser rendering so it is unit-testable with fakes/spies.
- **No heavy new audio assets assumed:** sounds are synthesised with the
  Web Audio `blip`/oscillator helpers already in `src/audio/effects.ts`
  `[ASSUMPTION]` (no binary asset pipeline in this repo).

## Existing state

- **Player-death particle burst already exists** (shipped in
  AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V, v0.1.3): `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y,
  SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry })`,
  called from `PlayScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()` and
  `GymFormationScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()`.
- **Sound:** both player paths call the generic enemy cue
  `playDestructionSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:430`, a 0.28 s descending
  sawtooth blip at volume 0.3). No player-specific cue exists.
- **Scale pulse:** both paths tween the ship to `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK` (1.5)
  over `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION/2` (0.2 s) and back.
- **No camera shake anywhere:** `grep` for `camera.shake` / `this.cameras`
  across `src/` returns nothing.
- **Two death paths:**
  - `PlayScene._hitPlayer() → _loseLife(explodeShip=true)` — costs a life,
    triggers `_finishRun(false)` at 0 lives, else `respawnInPlace()` +
    invulnerability blink.
  - `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` — combat gym: increments
    `playerHitCount`, plays sound + particles + scale pulse, `respawnInPlace()`,
    sets invulnerability/blink.
- Relevant constants live in `src/core/constants.ts`
  (`PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK=1.5`, `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION=0.4`,
  `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE=1.5`, `COMBAT_HIT_BLINK_INTERVAL=0.1`).

## Desired change

1. Add a shared player-death juice composition helper (pure severity→params
   mapping + thin Phaser application) in `src/vfx/`.
2. Add tunable constants for shake intensity/duration, flash alpha/duration,
   debris/shockwave counts/lifetimes, and severity multipliers, in one module.
3. Add a dedicated `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (layered, heavier) to
   `src/audio/effects.ts`; replace the generic `playDestructionSound()` call on
   the two player-death paths only (enemy paths unchanged).
4. Trigger scene-camera shake on player destruction, scaled by severity.
5. Add the extra juice layers (flash + debris/shockwave) as individually
   toggleable, teardown-tracked GameObjects.
6. Wire both `PlayScene._loseLife()` and `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` to the
   helper; preserve all existing non-VFX behaviour.
7. Add/extend unit tests and update GDD §7.2/§7.3 + comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — **new.** Composes shake + flash + debris/
  shockwave (+ delegates to existing particle helper); pure `resolveJuiceParams(severity)`
  mapping and teardown registry.
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` — **new.** Shake params, flash/debris
  lifecycle, severity scaling, teardown.
- `src/vfx/constants.ts` (or `src/core/constants.ts`) — new tunables:
  `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, debris/
  shockwave counts, `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (+ constants);
  leave `playDestructionSound()` untouched for enemies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_loseLife()` / `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the new helper with severity `'fatal'` vs
  `'respawn'`; SHUTDOWN teardown updates.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the helper with `'respawn'` severity;
  SHUTDOWN teardown updates (`playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene*.test.ts`
  — update/extend hit-response assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 particle/VFX and §7.3 audio notes.

## Related work

- **Immediate predecessor (completed):** Add particle-based explosion VFX for
  enemy and player deaths (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — delivered the shared
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`, colour jitter, three pattern emitters, and
  wiring to all death paths. Its scope-creep guard explicitly deferred
  **screen-shake, sound redesign, debris physics, and trailing smoke** to
  "linked work items if desired" — this item is that follow-up.
- Respawn player in same spot (AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN) — `respawnInPlace()`
  behaviour that must be preserved.
- Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT) — gym player
  presence.
- One Tank changes colour (AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G) — sibling colour-per-entity
  work; coordinates on palette usage.
- GDD §7.1 colour palette, §7.2 particle effects, §7.3 audio cues.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — "go wild" is unbounded / subjective.** Mitigation: bound the scope
  to a named layer set (shake, dedicated SFX, flash, debris/shockwave), each
  individually toggleable via constants; exact intensities are tunable and
  locked by unit tests, with a manual feel pass.
- **Risk — unanswered operator questions mean the layer set is a guess.**
  Mitigation: all invented scope is marked `[ASSUMPTION]`; the item is flagged
  `needsProducerReview`; each layer can be dropped without rework.
- **Risk — screen shake can cause discomfort / motion sickness.** Mitigation:
  keep duration short (~250–400 ms) and intensity modest; consider respecting
  a future reduced-motion setting (not in scope here — record as linked work
  item if the producer wants it).
- **Risk — test churn on hit-response suites.** Mitigation: update assertions
  to cover the new helper call/seams; keep behaviour guarantees (respawn,
  lives, no double-audio) explicit in tests.
- **Risk — double audio regression.** Mitigation: dedicated AC + test that the
  player path plays the new sound exactly once and not the generic cue.
- **Assumption — sounds are synthesised** via existing Web Audio helpers (no
  new asset pipeline).
- **Assumption — severity scaling** ('fatal' heavier than 'respawn') is wanted;
  easily removed if not.
- **Assumption — both death paths** (real run + combat gym) should get the
  juice; if only the real run is wanted, the gym wiring can be dropped.
- **Scope-creep guard:** reduced-motion accessibility setting, screen-edge
  vignette, controller rumble/haptics, score-popup redesign, and full audio
  redesign are out of scope; file as linked work items if desired.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Particle explosions already exist (completed in AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V). Do
  you want these enhanced (more particles, longer duration, additional effects
  layered on top), or is the particle part considered done?" — Operator replied

  assumption: single full-2D shake, intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms,

- Q3: "SFX — should the player death have its own dedicated sound distinct from
  enemy destruction? Layered sounds or a single improved sound?" — Operator
  replied "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption:
  dedicated layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()`, distinct from the generic
  enemy cue.
- Q4: "\"Lots of juice\" — beyond particles, screen shake, and SFX, what other
  juice do you envision? (e.g. screen flash, debris, slow-mo, UI feedback,
  score popup, camera zoom?)" — Operator replied "continue" without an answer.
  **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption: brief full-screen flash + debris

# Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does

## Problem Statement

Weapon power-up icons in AI Hell do not reliably convey what each weapon does. The clearest example is the rapid-fire weapon (P2), whose sine-wave icon reads as a slow, undulating line rather than a high-rate stream of bullets — it should use **stacked dots** that are visibly closer together than the slower forward-firing cannon. The producer has asked that **all** weapon icons be revisited and redesigned where the symbol does not match the weapon's behaviour.

## Users

- **Player**: Needs to identify what each weapon power-up does at a glance during fast, bullet-dense gameplay.
- **Player**: Needs the icons to make relative fire rates distinguishable (cannon 400 ms vs rapid 125 ms) without reading HUD text.

## Example User Stories

- As a player, I want the rapid-fire icon to show tightly **stacked dots** so it reads as a fast stream of bullets, not a slow wavy line.
- As a player, I want every weapon icon to visually reflect that weapon's actual firing pattern and relative rate, so I can learn the system quickly.
- As a player, I want the icon to be recognisable on both the field drop and the HUD.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Rapid icon uses stacked dots.** The rapid-fire weapon icon is redesigned as a stack of discrete circular dots (no singular sine/waveform line); the dots are tightly spaced so the icon reads as a rapid stream of bullets.
2. **Fire-rate distinction.** The rapid icon (125 ms, yellow) reads as visibly denser/faster than the cannon icon (400 ms, cyan) — the rapid stack has more, tighter-spaced elements than the cannon's single-bullet representation — so both forward-firing weapons are distinguishable at a glance.
3. **All weapon icons revisited.** Cannon, Spread, Dual and Rapid (plus the Reset drop) are each reviewed against their actual fire pattern/rate; each revised icon reflects its weapon's behaviour, with a one-line rationale recorded in code comments.
4. **Style and API preserved.** Icons remain code-drawn neon outlines (no external art assets) in `src/powerups/icons.ts`, drawn through the existing `drawWeaponIcon` / `drawWeaponDrop` API and `WeaponDropIconId` type; the glowing drop bubble, colours, and HUD integration are unchanged.
5. **Tests and validation.** Unit tests in `src/powerups/icons.test.ts` assert the updated icon geometry (e.g. the rapid icon emits multiple dot draw commands and differs from the other weapon icons); full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular the GDD §4.4 "Icon Suggestion" for P2 Rapid Fire ("Firing-rate waveform") and the icon-shape note in the GymWeapons implementation callout.

## Constraints

- **Code-first, no assets**: icons must be drawn with Phaser Graphics (GDD §7.1); no external images or fonts.
- **Neon aesthetic**: outlined shapes on black, matching existing `ICON_COLORS` / `WEAPON_ICON_COLORS`.
- **API stability**: `drawWeaponIcon` / `drawWeaponDrop` signatures and `WeaponDropIconId` must not change (used by field drops and HUD).
- **Scope**: the request covers **weapon** icons only (cannon/spread/dual/rapid/reset); non-weapon power-up icons (P3–P9) are out of scope.

## Existing State

`src/powerups/icons.ts` draws the weapon icons:

| Weapon | Colour | Icon (current) | Fire rate | Behaviour |
|--------|--------|----------------|-----------|-----------|
| Cannon | cyan | barrel line + bullet circle | 400 ms | single bullet straight ahead (permanent) |
| Spread | orange | three radial fan lines | 600 ms | 3-bullet fan (−30°/0°/+30°) |
| Dual | magenta | two parallel vertical bars | 500 ms | 2 parallel bullets (±8 px side offset) |
| Rapid | yellow | 4-cycle sine wave | 125 ms | single bullets at markedly higher rate |

The rapid icon's waveform metaphor does not read as "fast"; the producer has directed that it use **stacked dots**. Mixed metaphors across icons are explicitly acceptable (producer decision), so no single unified visual language is required — each icon should use the clearest metaphor for its weapon.

## Desired Change

- Redesign the **rapid** icon as tightly stacked dots.
- Re-review **cannon, spread, dual and reset** and adjust any icon whose symbol does not match its weapon's pattern/rate.
- Update the GDD §4.4 icon suggestion for P2 and the code comments in `src/powerups/icons.ts` to describe the new metaphors.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — Weapon icon drawing functions (`drawCannonIcon`, `drawSpreadIcon`, `drawDualIcon`, `drawRapidIcon`, `drawResetIcon`); primary change site.
- `src/powerups/icons.test.ts` — Geometry assertions for the redesigned icons.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — Weapon catalogue (fire rates, patterns, bullet colours/sizes) — reference for matching icons to behaviour.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpType` / `WeaponId` types.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Standalone HUD; renders weapon icons (should need no change if the API is preserved).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 icon suggestion for P2 and GymWeapons icon-shape note.

## Related Work

- **Migrated from** ContextHub work item `WL-0MTPL7K9E0025BWB` (misfiled in ContextHub; belongs to AI_Hell).
- **AH-0MTE8EB6Q007EU0J** — *Icons: code-drawn icons for P3, P4, P6, P7* (completed): established the code-drawn icon approach in `src/powerups/icons.ts`.
- **AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4** — *Power ups need to be larger* (completed): added the glowing drop bubble and larger drop rendering; added the current `icons.test.ts` geometry tests.
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** — *Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)* (completed): AC6 required code-drawn neon icons per GDD §4.4 shared by field drops and HUD.
- **AH-0MTCO0FYP008IR59** — *Standalone HUD class (attachable to any scene)* (completed): renders each active weapon's icon; relies on the preserved icon API.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Subjectivity**: icon clarity is partly subjective; "reflects the weapon" cannot be fully machine-verified. Mitigation: measurable proxies (dot count/spacing, geometric difference between icons) in unit tests.
- **Scope creep**: "revisit all symbols" could expand into a full visual redesign of every power-up. Mitigation: constrain to weapon icons (cannon/spread/dual/rapid/reset); record any non-weapon icon ideas as linked follow-up work items, not in this change.
- **Legibility at small sizes**: field drops and HUD rows render icons at different sizes; a dot stack must remain legible when small. Mitigation: test at the drop size and HUD size.
- **Assumption**: the existing `drawWeaponIcon` / `drawWeaponDrop` API is sufficient; no new icon types are needed.
- **Assumption**: mixed metaphors are acceptable (producer-confirmed), so no unification is required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

1. **Scope — rapid icon only, or all icons?**
   - Q: Should we only fix the rapid-fire icon (the concrete example given), or does the producer want all four weapon icons reviewed and potentially redesigned?
   - **Answer (producer, interactive reply)**: "revist all" — revise all weapon icons.
2. **Rapid icon metaphor**
   - Q: Should the rapid icon use more wave cycles (higher frequency sine wave), a different visual metaphor entirely (e.g. stacked dots, speed lines), or both?
   - **Answer (producer, interactive reply)**: "stacked dots" — use a stacked-dots metaphor.
3. **Visual consistency across icons**
   - Q: Should all weapon icons use a single visual metaphor (e.g. all bullets, all abstract symbols), or is the current mixed-metaphor approach acceptable with only the rapid icon improved?
   - **Answer (producer, interactive reply)**: "mixed is OK" — mixed metaphors are acceptable; no unification required.

- **AH-0MUCST2HU0097BIG** – Test: Choice strategy distinctness and permanent effects (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH** – Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, actual, added, adjust (+209 more)

The shipped game (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) and the gym core (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) each contain their own near-identical two-phase bullet/collision handlers (`_handleCollisions`). Producer directive on AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR: there should be no divergent core code between the shipped game and the gym scenes — they should share all code.

This item tracks extracting the shared combat/collision logic into a common module (or shared base) consumed by both, so future behaviour changes (e.g. the bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback delivered by AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR) cannot drift between the game and the gyms.

discovered-from:AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR

## Verified current state (2026-09-22)

Confirmed by direct inspection — the game and gym scene **do not** share a core engine:

- `PlayScene` (2 062 lines) and `GymFormationScene` (1 708 lines) are independent `extends Phaser.Scene` classes; no shared scene base exists and only these two files define `_handleCollisions`.
- 8 methods share names in both, average body similarity ~47 % (`_handleCollisions` 24 %, `_hitPlayer` 13 %, `_autoFire` 35 %, `_collectDrop` 37 %, `_spawnPlayerExplosion` 67 %, `_clearEnemyBullets` 0 %, `_handleTeleport` 100 %, `_readPlayerInput` 100 %).
- The handlers have **drifted**: `PlayScene` inlines boss multi-hit, asteroid splitting, mineral absorption and wave accounting; `GymFormationScene` uses generics + `config` callbacks and has no boss/asteroid/mineral paths.
- The entity/utility/service layer **is** shared (entities, powerups, audio, vfx, utils, core constants/rules) and both scenes import it.

## Problem
During parent/epic implementation, `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's feature branch to `refs/heads/dev` on the remote but does NOT fast-forward (or otherwise update) the local `dev` branch. The next `implement.py parent <epic>` call creates the next child's worktree from the stale local `dev`, so the new worktree is missing the just-merged sibling's files.

## Observed
- F2 (AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T) finish pushed commit 91538d0 to origin/dev; local dev stayed at 1920e65.
- The F3 worktree (AH-0MUBYXR280018HST) was created from local dev 1920e65 and could not resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local dev was fast-forwarded to origin/dev and merged into the worktree.

## Impact
Every child after the first can be created from a stale base, causing phantom build errors and risking lost/duplicated work. Workaround applied manually during the parent AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W run.

## Suggested fix
After a successful push in `phase_finish`, fast-forward the local parent branch to the pushed tip when the main checkout's parent branch is clean/unchanged (or at minimum, document the required manual `git fetch && git merge --ff-only origin/dev` step).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `implement.py finish` leaves local `dev` at least as advanced as the tip it pushed (when safe to fast-forward).
- [ ] A regression test covers the local-parent-branch update after a successful push.
- [ ] `implement.py parent` creates each child worktree from the up-to-date base.
